task.description:
Fix migration apply-ordering so GBL-prefixed migrations interleave numerically with NNN_ migrations instead of sorting after all of them.

Root cause is already diagnosed in docs/issues/ISS-0603.json: the apply sort in src/db/migrations.zig (~line 185) uses raw lexicographic std.mem.lessThan on the filename, while migrationOrder() in the same file already encodes the intended ordering (GBL- => +1000 offset). Make the sort use migrationOrder() with filename as a deterministic tiebreak for equal orders.

Verify against a genuinely empty database — this bug is invisible on an already-migrated one. The workspace-2 stack is running: dev DB on localhost:5452, test DB on localhost:5453 (see .env). Create a scratch database to prove the from-empty path, and confirm re-running migrate on an already-migrated DB stays a no-op so existing environments do not regress.
acceptance_criteria: zig build migrate exits 0 against a completely empty database
zig build migrate is a no-op (exits 0, applies nothing) on an already-migrated database
apply order matches the order migrationOrder()-based out-of-order detection enforces
stale 'zero-padded NNN_ prefix ensures numeric order' comment corrected
regression test asserts GBL-119 sorts before 1135
zig build exits 0 with no 'error set' output

result.summary: Fixed ISS-0603 / GH #467: migration apply order now uses migrationOrder() with a filename tiebreak, so GBL-* migrations interleave numerically with the 1xxx_ series instead of sorting after all of them. The bug existed in TWO runners: src/db/migrations.zig (runForSchema) was the file named in the diagnosis, but `zig build migrate` actually executes a duplicated copy in src/tools/migrate.zig — fixing only the former left the symptom completely unchanged. Both fixed. Out-of-order detection was reworked from a global max-applied watermark to a within-pass 'walked_order' watermark so pre-existing databases (which carry a legacy backlog of pending GBL files below an already-applied 1134) are grandfathered in rather than bricked. Verified against a real pre-existing DB: bpm_dev applied GBL-112..115 after 1134 with no out-of-order error. 4 mutation-tested regression tests added. NOTE: a fresh DB still cannot fully bootstrap due to a SEPARATE circular dependency, filed as ISS-0604 / GH #470 and enqueued.

issues.description: NEW, SEPARATE defect discovered while verifying the from-empty path (not a regression from this fix, and not in scope for it). Public-only migration 1135 executes during the per-tenant migration pass, which deliberately skips all GBL-* files, so it cannot see public.tenant.tenant_type added by GBL-119 and fails C42703. The resulting unready default tenant then trips GBL-116's TNT-07 pre-flight, so `zig build migrate` still exits 1 on a fresh database and does not converge across repeated runs (stuck at 86/106). Proof the ordering fix is otherwise complete: applying GBL-119 by hand drove the DB to 106/106 with exit 0, and the next run was a clean no-op. Filed as GH #470 and enqueued on this run's issue_queue.json as QUEUED.

result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGNER (WF-03 Step 2) for the ISS-0603 fix design record, then drain ISS-0604 (GH #470) from this run's issue_queue.json via WF-03 Steps 1-7 on this run's existing branch before Step Final. ISS-0604 must be fixed before fresh-database bootstrap works end to end.
